facts.condition: For any finite-auxiliary Marton law over two channel uses, strict improvement over twice the exact one-use randomized-time-division benchmark requires each coordinate input-one marginal to be in (0.375, 0.625), their sum to be in (0.85, 1.15), the aggregate cross-use output mutual information at the two receivers to be below 0.04375 bits, and the absolute input covariance to be below 0.175.

In the exchange-symmetric one-parameter input family whose two diagonal atoms have mass α and whose two off-diagonal atoms have mass 1/2−α, strict two-use Marton improvement requires α to lie in (0.125, 5/13).

assumptions: The canonical predecessor results supplying the two-use Marton upper-bound reduction and the exact randomized-time-division benchmark are valid and available.
The accepted result provides necessary conditions only; it neither constructs an improving law nor excludes all such laws.
